proves: The final statement of a list is deleted unless the language's overlay calls it terminating. In Go, a loop without a condition that a break ends, and a switch without a default clause, are not terminating, even when every clause of the switch ends in a return.
fixture: sum.prefix adds the values of a list before the first 0, in a loop without a condition that a break ends. grade sets a grade in a switch without a default clause, whose every clause ends in a return. Each is the final statement of its function.
